claim: Verbalized Sampling (ask for several responses with probabilities) raises diversity 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting in creative writing, with no training
quote: in creative writing, VS increases diversity by 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting
authors: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning, Shi
title: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
transfer: Divergence step: ask the model for a set of distinct candidates with stated likelihoods in one call, then pick from the set.

claim: Verbalized Sampling authors report more capable models benefit more, and say factual accuracy and safety are not hurt (claim only, no figures on abstract page)
quote: more capable models benefit more from VS
title: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
transfer: Use set-style divergence only on open tasks; keep single-answer tasks on one natural answer.

claim: CHECK: Verbalized Sampling is a single-group result. Search found no independent replication, and its page does not mention NoveltyBench. Verdict: promising for open tasks, unreplicated, and it does not explain why forced divergence stops helping on single-answer tasks.
title: Verbalized Sampling replication check
transfer: Treat as a hypothesis to test on our NoveltyBench arm.

claim: NoveltyBench finds top models produce far less diverse outputs than humans, and larger models in a family are less diverse than smaller ones
authors: Zhang, Diddee, Holm, Liu, Liu, Samuel, Wang, Ippolito
title: NoveltyBench: Evaluating Language Models for Humanlike Diversity
transfer: A single plain call collapses to one mode, so divergence steps have room to win on open tasks. Summary only, no verbatim span.

claim: NoveltyBench authors say in-context regeneration prompting helps somewhat but is not enough
title: NoveltyBench: Evaluating Language Models for Humanlike Diversity
transfer: Show the model its earlier answers and ask for something different; cheap divergence step.

claim: Self-certainty (the model's own output probability) can pick the best of N samples without a reward model, and also works on open-ended tasks where self-consistency voting is weak
quote: estimate response quality without requiring external reward models
title: Scalable Best-of-N Selection for Large Language Models via Self-Certainty
transfer: Needs token probabilities; check whether our API exposes them. If not, not usable.

claim: Universal Self-Consistency lets the LLM itself pick the most consistent of several samples, so it works for free-form answers; it matches standard self-consistency on math
quote: leverages LLMs themselves to select the most consistent answer among multiple candidates
authors: Chen, Aksitov, Alon, Ren, Xiao, Yin, Prakash, Sutton, Wang, Zhou
title: Universal Self-Consistency for Large Language Model Generation
transfer: One selection call over N drafts. Still same-model, so correlated samples limit it.

claim: For o1-like models, longer chains do not reliably help; correct answers tend to be shorter than wrong ones, and parallel sampling beats sequential revision
quote: longer CoTs of these o1-like models do not consistently enhance accuracy
title: Revisiting the Test-Time Scaling of o1-like Models
transfer: Cap thinking length; prefer several short parallel samples and prefer the shorter ones (Shortest Majority Vote).

claim: AdaptThink trains a reasoning model to choose think or no-think by difficulty; on math it cut length 53% and raised accuracy 2.4% for a 1.5B distilled model
title: AdaptThink: Reasoning Models Can Learn When to Think
transfer: Supports a router that skips deliberation on easy items. The method needs RL training, so we copy only the idea with a cheap difficulty check.

claim: Shojaee et al. report three regimes under equal inference compute: standard models win at low complexity, reasoning models at medium, both collapse at high
quote: we show that LRMs face a complete accuracy collapse beyond certain complexities
authors: Shojaee, Mirzadeh, Alizadeh, Horton, Bengio, Farajtabar
title: The Illusion of Thinking
transfer: Router rule: plain call for easy items, thinking for medium items.

claim: Lawsen's comment says Tower of Hanoi failures can come from output token limits, that scoring penalised practical limits, and that some River Crossing instances are unsolvable; asking for a generating function restored high accuracy
title: Comment on The Illusion of Thinking
transfer: Do not read collapse as a reasoning limit when the output is long. Let the agent write a program instead of listing steps.

claim: CHECK: Shojaee's collapse claim is contested. The rebuttal attacks the high-complexity collapse, not the easy-item result. Verdict: collapse contested, easy-item overthinking not rebutted in what I opened. Secondary blogs call Lawsen's output-limit evidence anecdotal and say falling token use on hard items is unexplained by it. Lawsen full text not read.
title: Shojaee vs Lawsen check
transfer: Keep the easy-item skip rule. Drop any rule built on a hard-item collapse threshold.

claim: Kamoi survey: no prior work shows successful self-correction using feedback from prompted LLMs, except on tasks suited to it; it works with reliable external feedback and with large-scale fine-tuning
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs
title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
transfer: Doubt step only with a real checker (tests, code run, retrieved fact).

claim: Huang et al.: LLMs struggle to self-correct reasoning without external feedback and sometimes get worse
quote: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback
authors: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet

claim: Self-Refine reports about 20% absolute average gain over one-step generation on seven tasks with GPT-3.5, ChatGPT and GPT-4
quote: Self-Refine does not require any supervised training data, additional training, or reinforcement learning.
title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
transfer: Gains may concentrate on style and preference tasks judged by humans or metrics; test only on open tasks.

claim: CHECK: Self-Refine vs intrinsic self-correction. Partly reconciled: Self-Refine gains come from mixed tasks scored by preference or metrics, while Huang and Kamoi concern reasoning with correctness labels. The oracle label leakage explanation rests on Huang's account, which I read only at abstract level. Verdict: task-type split plausible, leakage claim single-source, equal-token comparison not found.
title: Self-Refine reconciliation check
transfer: Allow refine on open tasks; ban it on single-answer tasks without a checker.

claim: CHECK: Equal-token comparison of CoT, self-consistency and Tree of Thoughts on modern models is NOT settled. The web search budget ran out before this query and I found no source I could open. The gap stays open; our own equal-cost runs remain the only evidence.
title: Equal-token comparison gap
transfer: Run it ourselves: same token budget for plain, best-of-N and scaffold arms.
